findings.title: `Integration.objects.get` in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` is not scoped to `provider='github'`
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` (line 478) and `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` (lines 494-496) look up `Integration` rows without filtering by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`. Because `Integration` uniqueness is on `(provider, external_id)` rather than `external_id` alone, if another integration provider has an `Integration` record with the same `external_id` (e.g. a numeric ID), `.get(...)` will either raise `Integration.MultipleObjectsReturned` (causing an unhandled 500) or match a non-GitHub integration.

findings.title: Direct access to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises `KeyError` when `sender` is absent
findings.body: At line 503, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes `"sender"` is always present in `integration.metadata`. However, `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (lines 376-377), so an existing `Integration` created through the pipeline (for example, one whose `OrganizationIntegration` was later deleted and is now being reinstalled, as in `test_github_installed_on_another_org`) will not have `"sender"` in `integration.metadata`. In that case, reinstalling raises an unhandled `KeyError` instead of completing or returning the error response.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` fails on OAuth state mismatch instead of testing a 404 installation lookup
findings.body: In `test_installation_not_found` (lines 379-396), the second request passes `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). As a result, `OAuthLoginView` rejects the request at the `state != pipeline.signature` check and returns `"Invalid installation request."` before `GitHubInstallation` or `build_integration` is ever reached, so the stubbed 404 response for `/app/installations/{installation_id}` is no longer exercised.
